cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: test coverage sits at 31%, there is no coverage gate in continuous integration, and production systems of comparable complexity typically run 40-60% coverage.
cases.output: Test coverage sits at 31%, with no coverage gate in continuous integration. This is below the 40 to 60% typically seen in production systems of comparable complexity, which means a regression can reach production unchallenged.

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: deployments are performed manually by one engineer via SSH, there is no rollback procedure, and the last rollback attempt (8 months ago) took over 3 hours to complete.
cases.output: The most recent rollback attempt, 8 months ago, took over 3 hours to complete, and deployments are performed manually by a single engineer via SSH with no documented rollback procedure.

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: one engineer holds sole access to the production database credentials, there is no documented access-handover process, and that engineer is on a rolling month-to-month contract.
cases.output: The production database credentials are held by a single engineer with no documented access-handover process, and that engineer operates on a rolling month-to-month contract. A departure—whether planned or sudden—would leave the company unable to access its own production database without an emergency rebuild. There is no compensating control. We recommend documenting the access-handover procedure immediately and moving credentials to a shared secret store with role-based access before the engineer's next contract renewal.

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: customer personal data is retained indefinitely with no deletion policy, and there is no documented process for handling a data-subject deletion request.
cases.output: Customer personal data is retained indefinitely with no documented deletion policy. There is no established process for handling a data-subject deletion request, which means the company cannot demonstrate compliance with deletion rights under data protection frameworks. This creates regulatory exposure and leaves the company unable to fulfill a legal obligation it will eventually face.

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) covering ALL of these facts: test coverage is 31%, there is no CI coverage gate, the last three production incidents were caused by untested edge cases, deployments are manual, and there is no rollback procedure. Do not omit any fact.
cases.output: Test coverage sits at 31%, with no coverage gate in continuous integration. The 3 most recent production incidents—all caused by untested edge cases—reveal the real cost of that gap. Deployments are performed manually with no documented rollback procedure, which means a regression that reaches production cannot be quickly reversed.

cases.input: Write three separate due-diligence findings, one paragraph each, clearly separated by a blank line. Finding 1 facts: passwords are stored in plaintext in the users table. Finding 2 facts: deployments are manual with no rollback procedure. Finding 3 facts: code comment style is inconsistent across the codebase, with no linting rule enforcing a convention.
cases.output:
Passwords are stored in plaintext in the users table, with no hashing or salting applied. Any compromise of database access—whether through SQL injection, insider access, or a backup restoration—exposes every user credential in the system. The company has no compensating control. This is a load-bearing gap at any scale, and customer accounts remain vulnerable to account takeover until credentials are hashed with a modern algorithm and existing passwords are reset.

Deployments are performed manually via SSH by a single engineer with no documented rollback procedure. The most recent production incident requiring a rollback took 45 minutes to reverse, during which the broken deployment remained live. Automation to stage changes, gate promotions, and execute rollbacks does not exist. A second operator has never executed the deployment workflow, so knowledge is concentrated and any absence or incapacity leaves the team unable to deploy or recover.

Code comments vary widely in style and content across the codebase, with no linting rule or team convention enforcing consistency. A new engineer joining the team receives no clear signal for what a comment should contain, where it should sit, or how formal the language should be. This is below the standard seen in similar codebases at the company's stage and makes onboarding slower and code review noisier. Establishing and automating a comment convention through a linter would bring this into line with peer systems.
